---
title: "CellPack and CP-BP"
---

## Purpose

CellPack compiles biological structure into execution geometry.

CP-BP is the current data-inferred block-packing implementation inside CellPack. It demonstrates that feature co-occurrence and bounded row coherence can be converted into compact, directly executable GPU tiles.

The current implementation should be preserved as the v1 baseline. Its objective, physical orientation, and operation coverage should not be mistaken for the final compiler.

## Current pipeline

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[Sample rows] --> B[Support bitsets]
    B --> C[Candidate discovery]
    C --> D[Exact merge-cost scoring]
    D --> E[Constrained optimizer]
    E --> F[Frozen packing plan]
    F --> G[Apply to full data]
    G --> H[Cell-block records]
    H --> I[Bounded row ordering]
    I --> J[Warp tiles]
    J --> K[Direct native consumer]
    J --> L[Persistent CPK1 image]
```

### Sampling and support

The compiler samples structural support rather than relying on value magnitude for its first v1 objective.

The fundamental binary observation is:

\[
A_{r,f} =
\begin{cases}
1 & X_{r,f} \neq 0 \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\]

Feature-major support bitsets make exact intersection, union, and overlap calculations efficient.

### Candidate discovery

Approximate similarity narrows the search space.

Candidate generation may use sketches or locality-sensitive hashing, but approximate similarity never decides the final merge. It proposes candidates for exact evaluation.

### Exact scoring

The v1 conceptual merge gain is:

\[
\operatorname{gain}(A,B)
=
\operatorname{cost}(A)
+
\operatorname{cost}(B)
-
\operatorname{cost}(A \cup B)
\]

The current default cost is tied to row-to-active-feature-block references.

This is a useful storage and scalar-execution surrogate. It is not the final end-to-end kernel objective.

### Optimization

The current host optimizer performs constrained deterministic moves with exact-oracle rollback.

This is valuable because it provides:

- reproducibility;
- exact local acceptance;
- durable packing-plan identity;
- a testable baseline;
- a clean seam for a replaceable cost policy.

### Frozen plan

The frozen plan records enough information to recover canonical feature identity:

- feature permutation;
- inverse feature permutation;
- feature-to-block map;
- feature-to-local map;
- block widths and offsets;
- plan identity;
- cost-policy identity;
- feature-axis identity.

That principle must survive.

### Applied plan and row order

The full partition is transformed into plan-relative feature blocks.

Rows are then reordered within bounded windows using active-block signatures. This exposes local sharing without allowing arbitrary global movement.

Bounded local ordering should remain a compiler tool, although its objective should become operation-aware.

### Cell-block records and warp tiles

Compact records encode active blocks and local masks without explicit zeros.

The current warp tile is row-oriented:

- up to 32 rows;
- block descriptors;
- participating-row masks;
- per-row local feature masks;
- compact values in rank order;
- dictionaries that recover canonical feature identity.

This is well matched to a lane-per-row scalar accumulation.

### Native execution

The direct v1 consumer proves that a CellPack image can be executed without reconstructing CSR or BELL.

That is the essential success criterion.

### Persistence

The current pointer-free CPK1 image contains:

- frozen plan maps;
- local row order;
- warp tiles;
- identities;
- offsets and lengths.

CellShard wraps the image in an opaque execution envelope and stages it contiguously. Cellerator validates and rebinds it.

## What CP-BP v1 proves

CP-BP v1 proves that:

1. biological co-occurrence can produce hardware-relevant geometry;
2. exact canonical identity can survive aggressive reordering;
3. a compact mask grammar can avoid explicit zeros;
4. construction can be separated from steady-state execution;
5. direct native consumption can beat CSR in structured regimes;
6. the same native path can lose in low-sharing regimes;
7. a planner therefore needs runtime plurality.

## What CP-BP v1 does not prove

It does not prove that:

- 32-row warp tiles are universal;
- row-major value order is best for `N > 1`;
- the v1 cost predicts training or sparse-to-dense ML;
- one semantic order serves every persistent workload;
- the current hardware model generalizes to real biological distributions;
- canonical output should follow every operation;
- CPK1 should be the only execution image;
- a matrix-wide format is optimal;
- Blocked-ELL or any vendor format is unnecessary.

## The target compiler

The target compiler produces semantic geometry first and physical projections second.

```text
observed biological structure
    + operation profile
    + biological priors
    + deployment profile
    + reuse profile
        ↓
candidate semantic geometries
        ↓
joint row, feature, module, and partition refinement
        ↓
validated semantic geometry
        ↓
physical projection candidates
        ↓
core planner and autotuner
```

## Semantic geometry

A semantic geometry contains:

```cpp
struct semantic_geometry {
    geometry_id identity;

    domain_id row_domain;
    domain_id feature_domain;

    order_id row_order;
    order_id feature_order;

    partition_id partition;
    hierarchy_handle hierarchy;

    canonical_recovery_maps recovery;
    geometry_statistics statistics;
};
```

It defines which biological entities execute together.

It does not require one physical layout.

## Multiple geometries

One geometry should be preferred when it serves the workload profile well.

A second semantic geometry is justified when:

- operation families are persistent and structurally incompatible;
- the cost of alternate ordered value planes is amortized;
- graph-wide conversion cost remains lower than forcing one compromise;
- training forward and backward benefit from substantially different partitioning.

Multiple geometries should be the exception, not prohibited.

## Physical projections

### Row-masked warp tile

Best candidate for:

- `N=1`;
- very small `N`;
- high block sharing;
- scalar regulatory reductions;
- memory-bound feature-weighted sums.

### Feature-major masked tile

Organize each active feature with a participating-row mask and compact values.

Best candidate when:

- one dense RHS row can be reused by several cells;
- `N` is larger than a scalar;
- feature-local propagation dominates;
- transpose-friendly access is valuable.

```text
tile
  feature id
  participating-row mask
  compact values by row lane
  next feature
```

### CTA macro-tile

Combine several neighboring row tiles.

Store:

- a deduplicated feature-block table;
- per-warp participation;
- feature-major records;
- compact values;
- optional dense fragments.

A CTA can stage a dense RHS slab once and share it across several warps.

### Dense fragments

Locally dense \(16 \times 16\) or similar regions may be expanded into MMA fragments.

The compiler records candidate fragments. The planner compares:

\[
T_{\text{masked}}
\quad\text{against}\quad
T_{\text{materialize}} + T_{\text{MMA}}
\]

Dense execution is selected only when the complete cost wins.

### Conventional fallbacks

CSR, SELL, BSR, and Blocked-ELL remain important.

They are especially useful for:

- low-sharing irregular regions;
- highly variable row lengths;
- vendor-supported shapes;
- broad `N`;
- one-shot operations;
- interoperability;
- reference and validation.

## Hybrid images

One structure may contain several region classes:

```text
high-sharing row-masked regions
feature-major regions
dense fragments
SELL or CSR residual
heavy-row queue
```

The projection constructor groups regions into class queues.

The runtime launches by queue or uses a persistent device work distributor. It does not perform a large host decision tree per tile.

## Operation-aware objective

The future compiler objective is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
J(G) =&\;
C_{\text{build}}(G)
+
C_{\text{persistent memory}}(G) \\
&+
\sum_o f_o
\left[
C_{\text{input order},o}
+
C_{\text{projection},o}
+
C_{\text{kernel},o}
+
C_{\text{epilogue},o}
+
C_{\text{output order},o}
\right] \\
&+
C_{\text{communication}}(G)
\end{aligned}
\]

where \(G\) is geometry and \(f_o\) is expected operation frequency.

The exact function may be a measured model rather than a closed analytical expression.

## Joint row and feature optimization

The biological structure is bipartite:

\[
G = (R,F,E)
\]

Feature blocks are good relative to rows that execute together. Row groups are good relative to the features they share.

A practical multilevel optimizer should:

1. initialize from support sketches and optional biological priors;
2. coarsen the bipartite or hypergraph;
3. construct capacity-constrained row and feature partitions;
4. refine feature groups given row groups;
5. refine row groups given feature groups;
6. construct nested CTA and GPU partitions;
7. classify physical regions;
8. evaluate measured or calibrated cost;
9. perform exact local rollback.

## Biological priors

Priors may include:

- pathways;
- regulatory programs;
- chromatin domains;
- enhancer-promoter groups;
- gene families;
- developmental lineages;
- known module membership;
- sequence-coordinate locality;
- previous model usage and gradients.

Priors are soft evidence.

A prior may improve stability, interpretability, and reuse. It may not override a severe measured execution loss.

## Statistics for near-zero-cost scheduling

A compact runtime tile header should contain only fields required by a kernel or queue.

Detailed compiler statistics may include:

- nnz;
- density;
- descriptor count;
- active rows;
- row-mask population;
- feature-mask population;
- lane-work variance;
- maximum row work;
- unique dense RHS rows;
- expected RHS reuse;
- metadata and value bytes;
- partial-block fraction;
- dense-fragment eligibility;
- heavy-row flags;
- active-module frequency;
- quantization range;
- forward and transpose locality;
- cross-partition edge count.

These statistics support planning without repeated structure scans.

## Hierarchical geometry

The same compiler may expose nested partitions:

```text
GPU partition
    biological supermodule
        CTA macro-tile
            warp tile
                local feature block
```

Nested partitions can reduce:

- global memory traffic;
- shared-memory duplication;
- launch fragmentation;
- inter-GPU communication.

Hierarchy should survive into the runtime image only when it changes execution.

## Persistence v2

The next execution image should have a projection directory.

```cpp
struct projection_directory_entry {
    projection_kind kind;
    std::uint32_t schema_version;

    structure_id structure;
    geometry_id geometry;
    projection_id projection;

    std::uint64_t offset;
    std::uint64_t bytes;
};
```

Structure and values should be independently bindable.

CPK1 remains readable through a v1 adapter identified as a row-masked projection.

## Training requirements

Training requires more than the forward tile.

The compiler must support:

- forward projection;
- transpose projection;
- logical edge identity;
- mapping between projection-local value orders;
- mutable value generation;
- gradient accumulation;
- optional fp32 master values;
- lower-precision execution values;
- optimizer update in execution order.

Dynamic topology changes create explicit structure epochs.

## Distributed geometry

The semantic geometry should permit nested ownership:

- row or cell partition;
- feature or module partition;
- sequence coordinate partition;
- hybrid partitions;
- replicated small modules;
- boundary-edge sections.

A distributed objective includes weighted cut cost:

\[
J_{\text{cut}}
=
\sum_{e \in \text{cut}}
f_e
\cdot
\operatorname{bytes}(e)
\cdot
\operatorname{topology cost}(e)
\]

The full distributed runtime can be deferred. The geometry ABI must not make it impossible.

## Acceptance criteria for a new CP-BP generation

A new generation is accepted only when:

- canonical identity remains exact;
- old images remain readable or a migration tool exists;
- the new objective is evaluated on real and adversarial structures;
- projection construction and amortization are measured;
- the planner selects it correctly;
- low-sharing and one-shot fallbacks remain strong;
- forward and backward implications are recorded;
- end-to-end biological work improves.

The goal is not a more intricate packer. The goal is less time per useful biological interaction.

## CE-GEO geometry outcome

The integrated path confirms the compiler boundary: CellPack/CP-BP produces
portable semantic organization and exact logical covers; an NVIDIA provider
performs target refinement and physical realization. The promoted V100 N=64
case uses an exact two-part physical cover—MMA-owned edges plus row-owned
residual edges—with stable logical recovery. No biological edge is pruned, and
padding is never treated as identity. Ten synthetic ablation families remain
calibration-only, including a retained correctness-negative showing that
dropped residual edges are invalid.
